Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
As always, changes contained herein do not go into effect for sanctioned tournaments for 30 days. (So these become active on October 5th, 2013 .)

Continental Championships Changes
Dropped: The "25%/33%/50% participants qualify" rule no longer applies. Added: "A player with at least 1 Game Win at a Continental Championship Qualifier qualifies." Added: "The winner of any Continental Championship Qualifier qualifies." Added: "For the Australian Championships, a player with at least 0.5 Victory Point per preliminary round played + 0.5 Victory Point qualifies." Added: "To reward the judges who put so much time and effort into running these events, the judges for Regional continental qualifiers automatically qualify if they don't play in their event."

==

The Archon
The Archon 1.5b has been finialized. It will be available in the  Download page.  (Please note we're still running validity checks against the upload module. Till October 5th, please continue to use the Archon available in the Download page.)
The Archon 1.5b should be compatible with OpenOffice and LibreOffice suites.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand

> the1andonlime wrote:
> Will the Asian and South American Continentals still remain open events after this change?

These tournaments, as long as they remain in Open format, are not affected by rules that affect the Qualification system.
Should their organizers decide to apply the Qualification system to their events, then, they would follow the rules given here (and there would have to be a choice on which system fits which event).

Messages.Author: BenPeal
Messages.Body:
> Dropped: The "25%/33%/50% participants qualify" rule no longer applies. Added: "A player with at least 1 Game Win at a Continental Championship Qualifier qualifies."
>
Is there a concern about players getting a GW in the first round and then dropping? (yay, re-doing seating...) Should players be required to play in all preliminary rounds of the qualifier without dropping/DQ'ing in order to be eligible to qualify?

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> Is there a concern about players getting a GW in the first round and then dropping? (yay, re-doing seating...) Should players be required to play in all preliminary rounds of the qualifier without dropping/DQ'ing in order to be eligible to qualify?
>
Hasn't been an issue so far (it would have mattered in "small" tournaments (in which a GW would lead you to the finals, thus awarding you the qualification slot).

It is not required that a partcipant has played in all rounds.
Especially:
- Players who couldn't attend the first round of the tournament, and have played rounds 2 and 3 successfully enough to get a GW will qualify.
- Players who made it to top 5 after preliminary rounds with a GW but drop the finals will still qualify.
- Players disqualified with no prize won't get their qualification at the event.
